result.summary: The image shows a one-way residential street with continuous sidewalks on both sides and parallel parking providing a buffer between pedestrians and moving traffic. While the environment appears low-speed, the upcoming intersection lacks visible high-visibility crosswalks and has potential sightline issues due to cars parked close to the corner.

hazards.name: Intersection Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles extend close to the intersection, potentially obscuring pedestrians and drivers from seeing each other.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs approaching the stop-controlled intersection in the background.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crosswalks
hazards.description: The intersection ahead lacks visible high-visibility crosswalk markings, which may reduce driver awareness of crossing pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: At the intersection with the stop signs in the distance.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20-30 feet of the intersection to improve sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install ladder or zebra-style crosswalk markings at the intersection to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and prevent illegal parking near the corner.

result.summary: This is a narrow residential street with row houses and a continuous sidewalk. A large street tree significantly narrows the effective walking path, and parallel parked cars on both sides create a visual barrier between the sidewalk and the roadway.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A large tree trunk occupies a significant portion of the sidewalk width, restricting the clear path for pedestrians, especially those with mobility aids or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image on the sidewalk

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on both sides of the narrow street limit visibility between pedestrians stepping off the curb and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the street

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Removing parking spaces closest to intersections to improve sightlines for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Adding curb extensions at intersections to shorten crossing distances and improve pedestrian visibility.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow, one-way urban street with continuous sidewalks and heavy on-street parallel parking on both sides. The environment lacks pedestrian safety infrastructure such as marked crossings or traffic calming, and parked vehicles create significant sightline obstructions for anyone attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Parked Vehicle Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the narrow street obscures pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the roadway along the entire block.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Crossings
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks or pedestrian warning signs are visible, which may lead to unsafe mid-block crossings.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at crossing points to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near potential crossing points to ensure clear sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Install vertical deflection measures to maintain low vehicle speeds appropriate for a residential/mixed-use street.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, well-maintained sidewalk separated from the roadway by a curb and a row of parallel-parked vehicles. The adjacent land use is dominated by a surface parking lot behind a chain-link fence, which creates a blank frontage and reduces natural surveillance of the walkway.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A continuous line of parked cars blocks the sight lines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the travel lane.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: The presence of a surface parking lot and chain-link fence creates a lack of active uses and 'eyes on the street', which can impact perceived safety.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping
interventions.description: Installing street trees in a dedicated furniture zone would provide shade, improve the aesthetic quality of the walk, and create a more substantial physical buffer from traffic.

interventions.title: Infill Development
interventions.description: Replacing surface parking lots with buildings that have active ground-floor uses would improve natural surveillance and the pedestrian experience.
